LanguageData.VV_Inspector_LureBaitReadyUnmet: Honey scent: wafting ({0} conditions not met)
LanguageData.VV_Inspector_LureNoBait: Honey scent: none (place honey, ambrosia or berries on it)
LanguageData.VV_Inspector_LureAwaitingSettlers: A band of vivis is expected in about {0}.
LanguageData.VV_Inspector_LureConditionMap: Vivis do not come to this map.
LanguageData.VV_Inspector_LureConditionRoyal: A royal vivi is already on this map.
LanguageData.VV_Inspector_LureConditionTemperature: It is too hot or too cold outside for vivis.
LanguageData.VV_Inspector_LureConditionWeather: It is dangerous to be outside now.
LanguageData.VV_Inspector_LureConditionUnreachable: The vivis cannot reach the structure from the map edge.
LanguageData.VV_Inspector_LureMissingRoom: No empty structure nearby with a door and a full roof.
LanguageData.VV_Inspector_LureMissingGrowingPeriod: The flowers here grow for too short a season to gather enough honey for the winter.
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_Idle: Waiting for visitors. When all visit conditions are met, visitors drawn by the honey scent will occasionally stop by; if the nest site conditions are also met, a band of vivis may follow the scouts and settle in.
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_NoRoyal: No royal vivi on the map
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_TemperatureTip: The outdoor temperature must be within a range that vivis wearing basic worker costumes can endure. Both the current temperature and the seasonal average are checked.
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_WeatherTip: Vivis do not come during toxic fallout, noxious haze or other conditions that make it dangerous to be outside.
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_BaitTip: Place honey, ambrosia, honey dishes, or berries on the lure to spread a sweet scent. Visiting scouts will sample a piece while inspecting the lure, whereas bears will devour it all.
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_NoOtherLure: No other lure in progress and no nest
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_FlowersTip: Counts flowers near the lure that yield honey. More flowers grant a higher score.
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_Room: Empty roofed structure with a door
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_RoomTip: Evaluates the most suitable structure near the lure. Rooms connected by doors count as a single structure. It must have a door and be fully roofed; structures that are too small or too large, connected to an owned bedroom or prison cell, or built on a gravship will not be used. Appropriately sized structures with fewer buildings inside (excluding arcane plants, pots, and lures) receive a higher score.
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_RoomReachable: Path from the map edge to the structure
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_FertileSoilTip: Counts unroofed fertile tiles near the lure that have no buildings. Settled vivis use this soil to grow cotton, roses, and arcane plants, as well as to dig up mana fertilizer.
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_GrowingPeriod: Growing period of at least {0} days
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_GrowingPeriodTip: Matches the growing period shown on the world map's terrain tab. Because a vivi nest gathers honey during the blooming season and relies on those stores to survive the winter, vivis will not settle in regions with a short growing period.
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_ManaTip: The concentration of environment mana near the lure. While not required, higher mana levels grant a higher score.
LanguageData.VV_ITab_ViviLure_ScoreTip: The combined score of nearby flowers, the structure, and environment mana (flowers have the highest weight, mana the lowest). A higher score attracts a larger band of vivis sooner.
LanguageData.VV_Letter_ViviLureScouts: {1} vivi(s) of {0} followed the honey scent of your lure.\n\nThey will inspect the lure, the surrounding flower beds, and nearby rooms. If they find the area suitable, a small band may return to settle here.
LanguageData.VV_Letter_ViviLureHornet: A titanic hornet has caught the honey scent of your lure and is flying toward it. Driven into a frenzy, it will attack anything nearby.
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviLureBear: {PAWN_definite} has caught the honey scent and is heading toward the lure.
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviLureScoutsFled: The vivi scouts left in a hurry. They will not report this place to their band.
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviLureScoutsDisappointed: The vivi scouts left without showing much interest.\n{0}
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviLureScoutsSatisfied: The vivi scouts were pleased with this place. A band of vivis may arrive soon.
LanguageData.VV_Letter_ViviNestSettlers:
A band of {1} vivis from {0} has arrived to settle in the empty room near your lure.

They will gather honey, pollen, and propolis from nearby flowers and trees, refine vivicream and viviwax, and build what they need on their own. Items they gather are marked forbidden, though you are free to take them.

The vivis do not mind your colonists passing nearby, but they quickly grow wary if anyone enters their rooms. If their wariness reaches its limit, they will turn hostile and abandon the nest. Forbid their doors or set allowed areas to keep your colonists out.
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviNestSettlersCanceled: The vivi band that was expected did not come.\n{0}
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviNestWary: The vivis of {0} are getting wary of your colonists in their rooms.
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviNestVeryWary: The vivis of {0} are very wary. Keep your colonists out of their rooms.
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviNestRescuedReturned: {PAWN_definite} has gone back to the nest, grateful for the rescue.
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviNestLeavingFew: The vivis of {0} are leaving: too few of them are left.
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviNestLeavingStarving: The vivis of {0} are leaving: they have been starving for too long.
LanguageData.VV_Message_ViviNestLeavingRoomLost: The vivis of {0} are leaving: their nest room is gone.
LanguageData.VV_Letter_ViviNestAlmostHostile: The vivis of {0} are about to lose their patience. If your colonists keep entering their rooms or harm them, they will turn hostile and leave.
LanguageData.VV_Letter_ViviNestHostile: The vivis of {0} have turned hostile and are fleeing their nest.
